Roofing in Pearland, Texas

Pearland spreads over three counties, and only one of them is in the state's coastal windstorm area. Call one free number any hour and you are put through to an independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Pearland calls.

Pearland roofing starts with one question: which county?

Roofing in Pearland, TX comes with a twist most homeowners never hear about until a bid arrives. The city covers parts of three counties, and only Brazoria County, where most of Pearland sits, is inside the Texas Department of Insurance coastal catastrophe area. That single line on the map decides whether a reroof needs a state windstorm inspection.

Pearland has grown fast. It incorporated in November 1959 with fewer than 2,000 people and counted 125,828 residents at the 2020 census, which makes it the largest city in Brazoria County. Much of that growth came in master planned communities west of State Highway 288 that are now reaching their first or second replacement roofs, often at the same time as their neighbors.

Houston Expert Roofers is a free phone line, not a roofer. Day or night, a recorded voice handles the first minute: it notes a quick description of the roof and your part of Pearland, and passes the call to an independent, locally owned roofing company that works here. That company does every part of the job and bills you for it.

Roofing work Pearland homeowners ask about

Pearland calls tend to come after weather: wind that lifted shingles, hail on a spring night, or water at the ceiling after a tropical downpour. Owners of homes from the early 2000s also call when the first roof starts to look tired. Each page below explains one kind of job.

Three counties, two sets of roofing rules

Find your county on your appraisal district record or tax statement, then read across. The city permit and the state windstorm program are separate things, and some Pearland addresses need both.

Where the house isCity of Pearland permitTDI windstorm inspectionWhat to settle with the roofer
Pearland, Brazoria County side (most of the city, including most of Shadow Creek Ranch)Yes, through the city's permit portalYes, Brazoria is on the first-tier coastal listWho files the permit, who schedules the windstorm inspection, and when you get the WPI-8
Pearland, Fort Bend County side (including part of Shadow Creek Ranch)YesNo, Fort Bend is outside the catastrophe areaThat the bid does not charge for a windstorm inspection you do not need
Pearland, Harris County side (the northern edge of the city)YesNoPermit filing and the scope of the job
Silverlake and other unincorporated Brazoria County land with a Pearland addressGenerally no, it is outside city limitsYes, still Brazoria CountyWhich office, if any, reviews the work, and who arranges the TDI inspection

In the windstorm area, the Texas Department of Insurance explains that a WPI-8 is issued for work inspected while it is under way, by an appointed Texas licensed engineer or a TDI inspector. Work that was never inspected during construction can only be certified afterward as completed work (a WPI-8-E) by a licensed engineer, so the timing of the inspection matters. TDI's Angleton field office handles Brazoria County.

Coastal windstorm rules. In the Texas Department of Insurance's designated catastrophe area (Brazoria, Chambers, Galveston and the other first-tier coastal counties, plus, in Harris County, Morgan's Point and the parts of La Porte, Pasadena, Seabrook and Shoreacres inside city limits and east of State Highway 146), roof work must meet the windstorm building code and be inspected while it is under way. When it passes, TDI issues a certificate of compliance (form WPI-8), which the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association uses to decide whether it can insure the home. Ask the roofer, in writing, who schedules the inspection and when you will get the WPI-8.

What the City of Pearland asks of a roofer

Pearland's Community Development department lists repairs to an existing structure among the work that needs a permit, and its contractor rules are specific. Contractors must be registered and have a contractor account with the city to apply for permits or schedule inspections. Their certificate of insurance must show at least $300,000 in general liability coverage and name the City of Pearland as the certificate holder.

That gives you a quick test. A roofing company already working in Pearland will have that account; a crew that arrived after the last storm may not. Ask before you sign, and ask the company to send its own certificate of insurance to you as well, since the city's copy protects the city, not your house.

The city's adopted codes include the 2021 International Residential Code, and its wind design criteria list an ultimate design wind speed of 150 mph. Applications, payments and inspection requests run through the city's Cityworks permit portal, and the city warns that it only collects permit fees in person at the City Hall annex or through that portal. Permit questions go to the city's permit office at 281-652-1638.

Storms that tested Pearland roofs

Harvey, 2017: a water story

A City of Pearland presentation reported structural flooding in more than 1,700 residences, much of it along Clear Creek. That was rising water, not roofs giving way, and it is covered by flood insurance, not a homeowners policy. It is still a reason to keep roof and flood paperwork apart after a storm that brings both.

Beryl, July 2024: a wind story

Community Impact reported local stations measuring winds above 70 mph, and an assistant police chief called it the worst damage since Hurricane Ike in 2008. Structural damage was limited, but trees and power took a beating, and the city council waived building permit fees for storm repairs.

Hail, May 2026: a fresh one

StormerSite, which compiles spotter and public reports, lists 1 inch hail in Pearland and 1.25 inch hail nearby on May 1, 2026, and counts 41 reports within 10 miles of the city since 2004. Hail that size can bruise shingles without leaving a visible hole.

Stay off the roof. Wet, storm-damaged roofs are slick and the decking may be weak, so leave the ladder in the garage. Keep well away from downed power lines and report them to CenterPoint Energy or 911. Indoors, move belongings away from the leak, put a bucket or towels under the drip and keep people out of any room where the ceiling sags. Photograph the damage from the ground and inside the house, then call your insurer and a roofer.

Why Pearland homeowners call the line

The windstorm step needs a local hand

On the Brazoria side, the inspection has to happen while the roof is open. Ask the company you reach how it schedules that inspection; a roofer that works here regularly will have a ready answer.

A registered company, not a passing crew

Pearland requires a contractor account for permits. A single call reaches a locally owned company, and you can confirm its city registration before anyone starts tearing shingles off.

Neighborhoods coming due together

Shadow Creek Ranch began selling homes in 2001, and Silverlake opened in 1995. When half a street needs roofs at once, an estimate based on your own roof is worth more than a door hanger.

No charge, any hour

Calling is free. If the roofer cannot answer right away, it receives your name, number, neighborhood and how urgent things are, and calls back. The company may pay the line a referral fee.

Shadow Creek Ranch, Silverlake and the HOA approval

Shadow Creek Ranch is the largest planned community in Pearland, about 3,500 acres west of State Highway 288 and south of Beltway 8; the city annexed the land in the late 1990s and home sales began in 2001. Because it straddles the Brazoria and Fort Bend County line, two neighbors can get bids that differ only because one needs a windstorm inspection. Silverlake, opened in 1995 with roughly 2,500 houses, sits just outside the city's western limits in unincorporated Brazoria County.

Both communities, like most Pearland subdivisions, have associations that approve roof color and style. Get the current guidelines before you collect bids. Texas Property Code section 202.011 stops an association from prohibiting impact-resistant or energy-efficient shingles that look like ones it already allows, which matters if hail makes a Class 4 shingle attractive. Ask your insurer whether such a roof changes your premium.

Questions to ask a Pearland roofing company

  • Is your company registered with the City of Pearland, with a contractor account in your name?
  • Which county is my house in, and does my job need a TDI windstorm inspection?
  • Who schedules that inspection, at what stage of the job, and when will I receive the WPI-8?
  • Which shingle, underlayment and fasteners will you use, and do they meet the windstorm requirements here?
  • What is your written price per sheet for damaged decking?
  • Who submits the HOA request, and which approved shingle does this estimate use?

Texas has no state roofing license. No state agency licenses roofing contractors in Texas, and a 2025 bill to create one (HB 3344) did not reach a vote of the full House before the session ended. So check what you can: a certificate of liability insurance sent to you, a written contract with the full scope, a permit where your city requires one, local addresses you can drive past, and the shingle maker's warranty registration. Some cities also ask roofers to register. The line does not check any of this for you. How to check a roofer before you hire.

The deductible is yours to pay. The Texas Department of Insurance says it is illegal for a contractor to offer to waive, rebate or absorb your deductible, and a contract of $1,000 or more paid with insurance money must include a notice saying so. A roofer also may not act as your public adjuster on a property it works on. Treat any offer to "cover the deductible" as a reason to call someone else.

For storm damage, read the roof insurance claims guide and keep the storm claim checklist close. In the Brazoria County part of Pearland, wind and hail coverage may come from the Texas Windstorm Insurance Association, which needs claims filed within one year of the storm. You file the claim; the roofer documents the damage.

Questions Houston homeowners ask

Do I need a windstorm certificate for a new roof in Pearland?

If your house is in the Brazoria County part of Pearland, very likely. Brazoria sits on the state's first-tier coastal list, the Texas Department of Insurance catastrophe area, so roof work there must meet the windstorm code and be inspected while it is going on, which leads to a WPI-8 certificate. The Harris and Fort Bend County parts of the city are outside that area. Your appraisal district record shows the county. The roof replacement page covers the rest of the job.

How do I pick a Pearland roofing company?

Begin with what the city requires. Pearland says contractors must be registered and hold a contractor account to apply for permits and schedule inspections, with a certificate showing at least $300,000 in general liability insurance that lists the City of Pearland as certificate holder. Ask the roofer to confirm it is registered, will pull the permit itself and, in Brazoria County, will arrange the windstorm inspection. The roofer check guide lists what else to ask.

Does a roof in Shadow Creek Ranch need a windstorm inspection?

It depends on the street. Shadow Creek Ranch is inside the City of Pearland, but most of it lies in Brazoria County and part of it in Fort Bend County. A home on the Brazoria side falls in the coastal catastrophe area and needs the windstorm inspection for TWIA eligibility; a home on the Fort Bend side does not. The city permit applies either way. Check your property's county before you compare bids, because it changes the scope.

Who permits a roof in Silverlake?

Not the City of Pearland, in most cases. Silverlake is a planned community in unincorporated Brazoria County, outside Pearland's western city limits and partly within the extraterritorial jurisdictions of Pearland and Manvel. Because it is in Brazoria County, the state windstorm rules still apply to roof work. Ask the roofer which office, if any, reviews the job, and who will schedule the TDI inspection.

Who actually does the roofing if I call from Pearland?

An independent, locally owned roofing company that takes Pearland calls. Houston Expert Roofers is only a number and a website. A recorded assistant asks about the roof and your part of Pearland, then passes the call to that company, which inspects, prices, permits and builds the roof and bills you itself. You pay nothing to call; the company may pay the line a referral fee.
